risk.title: Risk check

sex.q: Are you a man or a woman?

age.help: This check is for adults 18 and older.

height.help: If you don't know, stand against a wall, mark the top of your head, and measure from the floor.

weight.help: Use a scale at home, a pharmacy or a health centre.

waist.help: Use a string: wrap it around your belly at the level of your belly button, breathe out normally, mark the string, then measure it with a ruler or tape. You can also use your trouser waist size as a rough guide.

activity.q: Do you do at least 30 minutes of physical activity every day?
activity.help: This includes physical work, walking, cycling, farming or exercise.

vegFruit.q: Do you eat vegetables or fruit every day?

bpMeds.q: Have you ever taken medicine for high blood pressure?

highGlucose.q: Has a health worker ever told you that your blood sugar was high?
highGlucose.help: For example at a check-up, while you were sick, or during pregnancy.

family.q: Has anyone in your family had diabetes?
family.second: Yes: grandparent, aunt, uncle or cousin
family.first: Yes: parent, brother, sister or my own child

smoker.help: Cigarettes, hand-rolled tobacco or other smoked tobacco.

sbp.q: Do you know your blood pressure?
sbp.help: Blood pressure is written like 130/80. Enter the top (bigger) number from a recent measurement.

nextSteps.see_doctor_soon: Visit a doctor or health centre in the next few weeks for a check-up. Show them these results.
nextSteps.glucose_test: Ask a health centre for a blood sugar test.
nextSteps.check_bp: Get your blood pressure measured at a health centre or pharmacy, then check again.
nextSteps.healthy_habits: Keep up healthy habits and check again in about a year.
nextSteps.cholesterol_test: Ask a health centre for a blood cholesterol test, then check again.
nextSteps.cvd_followup_5_10: Visit a health centre for advice on food, exercise, smoking and alcohol. WHO advises a check-up every 3 months until your targets are met, then every 6 to 9 months.
nextSteps.cvd_followup_10_20: Visit a health centre for advice and to check your blood pressure. WHO advises a check-up every 3 to 6 months.
nextSteps.cholesterol_very_high: Your total cholesterol is 8 mmol/L (320 mg/dL) or more. WHO advises that a doctor considers treatment for this. Visit a doctor or health centre in the next few weeks and show them this result.
nextSteps.tb_test: Go to a health centre and ask for a TB test. Tell them which symptoms you have. This check is not a diagnosis: many people with these symptoms don't have TB, but only a test can tell.
nextSteps.tb_contact_check: Go to a health centre, tell them you live with or are close to someone who has TB, and ask to be checked. WHO says close contacts of people with TB should always be screened.
nextSteps.tb_watch: A symptom check misses about 3 in 10 people with TB. If you get a cough, fever, night sweats or weight loss, go to a health centre and ask for a TB test.
nextSteps.bp_very_high: Your reading is 160/100 or higher. WHO says that when blood pressure is this high, treatment should start without delay. Visit a doctor or health centre as soon as you can and show them this reading.
nextSteps.bp_recheck: This reading is 140/90 or higher. One reading is not a diagnosis: high blood pressure is confirmed when it is high on two different days. Get it measured again on another day at a health centre.
nextSteps.bp_pregnancy: In pregnancy, a reading of 140/90 or higher needs to be checked by a doctor or midwife soon. WHO says high blood pressure in pregnancy must be diagnosed and followed up carefully.
nextSteps.bp_above_target: Your reading is above the WHO treatment target of below 140/90. Talk to your health worker about your treatment. WHO suggests a check every month after a medicine change until you reach the target.
nextSteps.bp_above_target_130: Because you have heart disease, diabetes or kidney disease, WHO's target for the top number is below 130. Your reading is above that. Talk to your health worker about your treatment.
nextSteps.bp_high_risk_130: Your top number is 130–139. Because you have heart disease, diabetes or kidney disease, WHO advises that a health worker considers treatment at this level. Show them this reading at your next visit.
nextSteps.bp_at_target: Your reading is within the WHO treatment target. WHO suggests a check every 3 to 6 months while your blood pressure is under control.
nextSteps.bp_below: This reading is below 140/90, the level at which WHO recommends treatment. To keep it healthy: less salt (under 5 g a day), more fruit and vegetables, regular activity, no tobacco and less alcohol.

about.title: About SokhaPheap
about.body: SokhaPheap helps adults in Cambodia understand their risk of type 2 diabetes and heart disease early, explains blood test results in simple language, and shows the nearest health facilities using Cambodian open data. It was built for the Open Data × AI Venture Hackathon, Phnom Penh, 2026.
about.how1: Diabetes risk uses the FINDRISC questionnaire (Finnish Diabetes Risk Score).
about.how2: Heart risk uses the WHO 2019 non-laboratory cardiovascular risk chart for South-East Asia.
about.how3: Scores are calculated by fixed rules, not by AI. AI is only used to read lab report photos and to explain results in simple words.
about.limit1: These scores were developed outside Cambodia and have not been validated in Cambodia yet.
about.limit2: Part of the facility data is from 2010. Some facilities may have moved, closed or changed.
about.limit3: Lab normal ranges vary between laboratories. We use the range printed on your report when there is one.
about.privacy: We do not ask for or store your name, phone number or ID. Lab photos are deleted right after reading. Risk results are saved without any personal details, for anonymous statistics.
about.how4: Open Data Insights combines 12 Cambodian and international open datasets into a Screening Gap Index that shows where people are most at risk and furthest from care. Your results show facts about your area from the same data.
about.roadmap1: Keep facility data current: replace the Ministry of Health 2010 facility list with newer official data when it is published, and refresh the OpenStreetMap health facilities (HOT export) every month.
about.roadmap2: Add province-level blood pressure and blood sugar data from the next Cambodia Demographic and Health Survey or WHO STEPS survey, so the gap index can include them.
about.roadmap3: Refresh travel times each year with the Malaria Atlas Project and HeiGIT accessibility data, and population with WorldPop and the National Institute of Statistics (COD-PS).
about.roadmap4: Use WFP market prices to give affordable healthy food tips in every province, and work with NGOs to check the Screening Gap Index against real screening results.
about.insightsLink: See the Open Data Insights page

method.title: How the Screening Gap Index works
method.p1: We combine five parts, each scored from 0 (smallest gap) to 1 (biggest gap) across all districts:
method.risk: Risk factors: women overweight or obese, men and women who smoke (DHS 2021–22, province level).
method.access: Distance to care: average travel time by car or motorbike, people more than an hour's walk from care (Malaria Atlas Project 2019 with WorldPop 2025), and women who say distance is a problem (DHS).
method.capacity: Few facilities: health facilities per 10,000 people (Ministry of Health 2010 and OpenStreetMap 2026, with WorldPop 2025).
method.people: Many adults: estimated adults aged 20+ (WorldPop 2025 and official 2024 age structure).
method.poverty: Poverty: people in the poorest fifth of households (DHS 2021–22).
method.p2: Each number is capped at the 5th and 95th percentile and scaled from 0 to 1. The five parts have equal weight. The index is their average × 100, so it runs from 0 to 100. The three parts that add the most are shown as the main reasons.
method.l1: Survey figures exist only per province, so all districts in a province share them, and they cover ages 15–49 only.
method.l2: Travel times are modelled for 2019 and may be different today. Facility data is partly from 2010.
method.l3: There is no province-level data on blood pressure or blood sugar, so these are not in the index.
method.l4: Changing the method changes the ranking. Our sensitivity check keeps 8 of the top 10 districts in a typical variation.

apiDocs.title: Open data API
apiDocs.intro: SokhaPheap gives its processed open data back to everyone. These read-only endpoints return JSON. No key is needed.
apiDocs.licence: Licence: CC BY 4.0. Please cite: SokhaPheap open data (2026), derived from COD-AB, COD-PS, WorldPop, Malaria Atlas Project, Ministry of Health, OpenStreetMap, DHS 2021–22 and WHO.
apiDocs.limits: Limits: 60 requests per minute per user. Responses are cached for 1 hour. Data is updated when the pipeline is rebuilt.
apiDocs.areasDesc: Every province or district with population, travel times, facilities, DHS indicators (province values) and the Screening Gap Index.
apiDocs.areaDesc: One area by P-code: province (KH12), district (KH1201) or commune (KH120101). Communes include the nearest hospital and health centre.
apiDocs.sourcesDesc: Every dataset used, with publisher, licence, data year and SHA-256 hashes of the raw files.
apiDocs.downloadsDesc: District table (CSV) and gap index map (GeoJSON), also CC BY 4.0.
fields: travel_motor_mean_min / travel_walk_mean_min: population-weighted minutes to the nearest health facility (Malaria Atlas Project 2019)
pct_walk_over_60_min / pct_motor_over_30_min: share of people beyond 1 hour on foot / 30 minutes by car or motorbike
facilities, facilities_per_10k: facility counts by type (Ministry of Health 2010 + OpenStreetMap 2026)
gap: Screening Gap Index (0–100), rank, component scores and main drivers
apiDocs.note: Area data describes populations, not individuals. The gap index is a planning tool, not a measure of anyone's health.
